title: Atlas · Tue Nov 17 · 6:45am
big_picture: Taylor, prices below are yesterday's close (Mon Nov 16); the open is 7:30am. Futures were mixed this morning: Dow and S&P slightly lower, Nasdaq slightly higher, after Monday's sharp drop (SPY -1.9%) ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-november-17-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-nvidia-earnings-091546152.html)). Nvidia reports after the 2:00pm close today, and it is the first report since Jensen Huang left; interim CEO Colette Kress will be on the call. Premarket reports on Nvidia differ (between +1% and -0.5%, captured at different times), so I would not read anything into it ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/nvidia-stock-earnings-jensen-huang-resignation.html), [TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262308986-nvidia-earnings-ai-chip-remote-access-restrictions-tradingkey)). Consensus is about $108.8B revenue and $2.47 EPS; the watch points are Blackwell shipments, margin, the Q4 guide and Nvidia's financial support for AI customers ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/11/63337722/nvidia-earnings-preview)). The export rule that hit chips Monday is now confirmed as an interim final rule from Commerce's BIS: licences for advanced chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, plus limits on remote access for China-headquartered firms; reports say US cloud firms that meet reporting duties are exempt ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-16/us-moves-to-limit-remote-access-to-advanced-ai-chips), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nvidia-jensen-huang-commerce-department-limit-remote-access-ai-chips/)). One outlet puts customers in those five countries at no more than 1.3% of Nvidia revenue, citing its filing; I could not check that figure ([Techi](https://www.techi.com/us-ai-chip-export-rule-nvidia-revenue-exposure/)). Home Depot beat (EPS $3.86 vs $3.84, revenue $43.4B vs $42.81B) and named its CFO as the next CEO; Disney beat too (EPS $1.77 vs $1.68) ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/long-ideas/26/11/63331751/walt-disney-nvidia-and-3-stocks-to-watch-heading-into-tuesday)). Brent was about $93 and spot gold about $3,860 in one pre-open snapshot, so approximate.
